tools_helpful.evidence: Turn 47: validator ran residue grep, mapping-consistency, dotnet build, smoke launch, visible-text fidelity and reported PASS, giving the agent a single go/no-go gate before finishing.
Bulk Windows.UI.Xaml -> Microsoft.UI.Xaml rewrite left only a handful of code-level errors to fix by hand (Turns 38-45).

tool_limitations.limitation: Runs only after the project already builds, so it cannot guide the build-fix loop where CS0104 / WMC cascade errors occur.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Keep the build-error interpretation guidance in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md (prose), where the agent reads it during the fix loop.

failed_apis.why_tried: UWP Scenario7_B2B.xaml.cs uses unqualified HttpClient from `using Windows.Web.Http;`
failed_apis.root_cause: In a WinUI 3 .NET project System.Net.Http is also in scope, so unqualified HttpClient/HttpResponseMessage become CS0104 ambiguous between System.Net.Http.* and Windows.Web.Http.*.

special_apis.special_handling: Common UWP HTTP namespace; collides with System.Net.Http after migration. Fully qualify or alias.

errors_encountered.error: CS0104: 'HttpClient' is an ambiguous reference between 'System.Net.Http.HttpClient' and 'Windows.Web.Http.HttpClient' (Scenario7_B2B.xaml.cs, Turn 38)
errors_encountered.root_cause: UWP code used unqualified HttpClient resolved from `using Windows.Web.Http;`; WinUI 3 .NET also exposes System.Net.Http, creating the ambiguity.

errors_encountered.error: WMC0909: Cannot resolve DataType local:Scenario + WMC1111 (DataTemplate x:Bind needs x:DataType) in MainPage.xaml (Turn 38), preceded by WMC1509 'No LocalAssembly parameter given during MarkupCompilePass2'.
errors_encountered.root_cause: The 6 CS0104 C# errors prevented the project assembly from compiling, so the XAML markup pass 2 had no LocalAssembly (WMC1509) and could not resolve the perfectly-valid project-local type `Scenario` referenced by x:DataType -> spurious WMC0909/WMC1111.
errors_encountered.fix: Agent downgraded x:Bind/x:DataType to {Binding} (Turn 39). This silenced the error but was unnecessary: fixing the C# CS0104 errors and rebuilding would have cleared the markup-pass errors too, keeping compiled bindings.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: 6 build errors: CS0104 HttpClient/HttpResponseMessage ambiguity + WMC0909/WMC1111 x:Bind DataType resolution + WMC9999 internal error.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: 2 build cycles (Turn 38 fail -> Turn 39 fixes -> Turn 40 succeeds)
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: CS0104 = System.Net.Http vs Windows.Web.Http ambiguity not documented in the skill's CS0104 section (which only covers the Windows.UI.Xaml vs Microsoft.UI.Xaml axis). The WMC errors were a cascade of the C# compile failure (WMC1509 LocalAssembly missing).
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Fully qualified the Http types; separately switched the scenario-list DataTemplate from x:Bind to {Binding}.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Extend the CS0104 pattern to cover System.Net.Http vs Windows.Web.Http; add a note that XAML 'cannot resolve DataType/local type' (WMC0909/WMC1111 with WMC1509) errors are usually a cascade of C# compile errors — fix C# first, rebuild, do not downgrade x:Bind to {Binding}.

env_issues.workaround: Scoring fell back to per-scenario UIA trees; migration skill already avoids system backdrop / ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar to reduce blanking. No migration action needed.
